summary: Murchison tower on Highway 60 in Nipissing District: on a 1963 Lands and Forests map and one of 15 Pembroke district lookouts; no source gives its condition today.

facts.agency: Ontario Department of Lands and Forests, later the Ministry of Natural Resources

staffing.status: staffed in the 1960s, per a researcher's cousin's account on Firelookout.ca

events.note: Appears on the Department of Lands and Forests Tower Detection System Map (1963), as Firelookout.ca cites it; a map record, not a build date
Pembroke Forest Fire District founded; Wikipedia lists Murchison among its 15 lookouts. This is the district's founding date, not the tower's
Wikipedia says the district's towers were expected to be phased out after aerial firefighting methods were adopted in the 1970s; decade only, no Murchison-specific date

evidence.supports: Location on Highway 60 in South Algonquin Township, Nipissing District
evidence.quote: Highway 60, South Algonquin Township, Nipissing District, Northeastern Ontario, Ontario, K0J 2C0, Canada

evidence.supports: Elevation of 514 m (1686 ft); this is ground elevation, not tower height
Tower appears on the 1963 Department of Lands and Forests tower map
evidence.quote: Appears on the Department of Lands and Forests Tower Detection System Map (1963).

evidence.supports: A researcher's cousin worked in the tower during the 1960s (single anecdote)
evidence.quote: cousin worked in this tower in the 1960

evidence.supports: Pembroke Forest Fire District set up by the Department of Lands and Forests in 1922 as one of 17 districts
evidence.quote: Department of Lands and Forests (now the MNR) in 1922 as one of 17 districts
The headquarters for the district were housed in the town.

evidence.supports: Pembroke district was the central location for 15 fire tower lookouts
evidence.quote: It was the central location for 15 fire tower lookouts, including the towers in Algonquin Park.

evidence.supports: Murchison is named among the 15 lookouts
evidence.quote: The 15 towers included: Wilberforce, Mt. Edna, Sherwood, Murchison, Preston

evidence.supports: Towermen took bearings from their towers and radioed headquarters
evidence.quote: a towerman would get the degree bearings from his respective tower and radio back the information to headquarters

evidence.supports: Plotting the exact location of a fire needed bearings from one or more other towers as well
evidence.quote: When one or more towermen from other towers in the area would also call in their bearings

evidence.supports: Headquarters could plot the exact location of a fire from several bearings
evidence.quote: plot the exact location of the fire on their map

evidence.supports: District towers were to be phased out after aerial firefighting came into use in the 1970s
evidence.quote: These towers would all be phased out after aerial fire fighting techniques were employed in the 1970s.

notes_for_editor: Firelookout.ca gives an elevation (514 m), not a tower height; no source gives height, build date, design, current status or access. Staffing rests on one anecdote in the Firelookout.ca entry (a researcher's cousin). The 1922 date is the Pembroke district's founding, not the tower's. The phase-out sentence covers the district's towers generally, so the story says they were 'to be' phased out rather than naming Murchison. Wikipedia was used for district facts as a lead; its own citations for the Forest Fire Protection History section were not checked and should be before publication. Brief status and access were 'unknown' and are left unset; no source describes the site today. Confidence medium: two independent sources place the tower in the district and on the 1963 map, but nothing on condition or access.
